altshiller-court.name: Altshiller-Court, Nathan
altshiller-court.bio: Polish-born, Belgian-educated mathematician (D.Sc., University of Ghent, 1911) who taught at the University of Oklahoma for over thirty years. His College Geometry (1925; 2nd ed. 1952) and Modern Pure Solid Geometry (1935) established the standard English-language synthesis of modern synthetic triangle and circle geometry.
works: Mathematics in Fun and in Earnest (1958)

apollonius.name: Apollonius of Perga
apollonius.bio: Author of the Conics and lost treatises Plane Loci (reconstructed by Robert Simson, 1749) and Tangencies (On Contacts, reconstructed by Viète, 1600). Namesake of the Apollonian circle of constant distance ratio (§ 11, Locus 11), the three Apollonian circles of a triangle (Ch. X, § 597), and the Problem of Apollonius on circles tangent to three given circles (Ch. VIII, §§ 506–517).

archimedes.name: Archimedes of Syracuse
archimedes.bio: Greatest mathematician of antiquity, cited by Altshiller-Court for theorems on chords, circles, the arbelos (shoemaker's knife), and precursors to harmonic and metric relations.

bernhart.name: Bernhart, Arthur
bernhart.bio: Colleague of Nathan Altshiller-Court in the Department of Mathematics at the University of Oklahoma; acknowledged in the 1952 Preface/Acknowledgments (p. ix) for reading the proofs of the Second Edition.

bobillier.name: Bobillier, Étienne
bobillier.bio: Early contributor to projective and metric triangle geometry, abbreviated geometry of polars, and pedal/circumcircle properties.

brahmagupta.name: Brahmagupta
brahmagupta.bio: Formulated the area formula and orthogonality/median-altitude theorem for cyclic quadrilaterals with perpendicular diagonals (Brahmagupta's theorem, Ch. IV).

brianchon.name: Brianchon, Charles Julien
brianchon.bio: Student at the École Polytechnique under Monge. With Poncelet (1821), published the first complete proof of the Nine-Point Circle theorem and discovered Brianchon's hexagram theorem.
works: Recherches sur la détermination d'une hyperbole équilatère (with Poncelet, 1820–1821)

brocard.name: Brocard, Henri
brocard.bio: Co-founder (with Lemoine and Neuberg) of the late-19th-century revival of triangle geometry. Investigated the Brocard points Ω, Ω', Brocard angle ω, Brocard circle, and Brocard triangles (Ch. X, §§ 649–683).
works: Étude d'un nouveau cercle du plan du triangle (1881)
Notes de bibliographie des courbes géométriques

butchart.name: Butchart, John Harvey
butchart.role: Professor of Mathematics, Arizona State College
butchart.bio: American geometer and contributor to The American Mathematical Monthly; acknowledged by Altshiller-Court (p. ix) for carefully reading both the manuscript and the proofs of the 1952 Second Edition and contributing important suggestions and additions.
works: Some Properties of the Limaçon and Cardioid (Amer. Math. Monthly, 1945)

carnot.name: Carnot, Lazare Nicolas Marguerite
carnot.bio: Pioneered the systematic use of signed geometric quantities and transversals in Géométrie de position (1803); proved Carnot's Theorem relating circumradius, inradius, and signed distances from circumcenter to triangle sides (§ 146).
works: Essai sur la théorie des transversales (1806)

casey.name: Casey, John
casey.role: Irish Geometer, Catholic University of Ireland
casey.bio: Author of A Sequel to the First Six Books of the Elements of Euclid (1881), one of the primary English precursors to College Geometry. Formulated Casey's Theorem (§ 471), generalizing Ptolemy's theorem to four circles tangent to a fifth circle, leading to an elegant proof of Feuerbach's theorem.
works: A Sequel to the First Six Books of the Elements of Euclid (1881; 6th ed. 1892)

castillon.name: Castillon, Johann (Salvemini, Giovanni Francesco)
castillon.bio: Solved in 1776 the celebrated Cramer-Castillon Problem of inscribing in a given circle a triangle whose sides pass through three given points—a projective-constructive counterpart to Chapter I's incidence problems (§ 9, § 14).
works: Sur un problème de géométrie plane (Nouveaux Mémoires de l'Académie de Berlin, 1776)

catalan.name: Catalan, Eugène Charles
catalan.bio: Author of Théorèmes et problèmes de géométrie élémentaire (`Cn.` in Altshiller-Court's bibliography), a rich treasury of constructive problems, harmonic division, and coaxal systems.
works: Théorèmes et problèmes de géométrie élémentaire (6th ed., 1879)

ceva.name: Ceva, Giovanni
ceva.bio: Discovered Ceva's Theorem (1678) governing the concurrency of triangle cevians via products of signed ratios on the sides (Ch. VI, § 326).
works: De lineis rectis se invicem secantibus statica constructio (1678)

chapple.name: Chapple, William
chapple.bio: Published in 1746 (twenty years before Euler) the formula d² = R(R - 2r) for the distance between the circumcenter and incenter of a triangle (§ 152).
works: An Essay on the Properties of Triangles Inscribed in and Circumscribed about Given Circles (1746)

chasles.name: Chasles, Michel
chasles.bio: Master of projective geometry, cross-ratios (anharmonic ratio), homography, and the history of synthetic methods (`Chl.` in Altshiller-Court's bibliography).
works: Aperçu historique sur l'origine et le développement des méthodes en géométrie (1837)

coolidge.name: Coolidge, Julian Lowell
coolidge.bio: Author of A Treatise on the Circle and the Sphere (1916), synthesized by Altshiller-Court in Chapters VIII–X.
works: A Treatise on the Circle and the Sphere (1916)

court-arnold.name: Court, Arnold
court-arnold.role: Climatologist & Professor of Geography, UCLA / CSUN
court-arnold.bio: Son of Nathan and Sophie Altshiller-Court; renewed the copyright of the 1952 Second Edition of College Geometry in 1980 (p. [iv]).

crelle.name: Crelle, August Leopold
crelle.bio: Early investigator (1816) of the Brocard points and angle inside a triangle sixty years before Brocard's 1875–1881 rediscovery.
works: Über einige Eigenschaften des ebenen geradlinigen Dreiecks (1816)

desargues.name: Desargues, Girard
desargues.role: French Architect & Founder of Projective Geometry
desargues.bio: Introduced points and lines at infinity, involution, polar reciprocity, and Desargues' Two-Triangle Perspective Theorem (§ 343).
works: Brouillon project d'une atteinte aux événemens des rencontres du cône avec un plan (1639)

descartes.name: Descartes, René
descartes.bio: Founder of analytic geometry; contrasted by Altshiller-Court with pure synthetic and Greek geometric analysis.

docagne.name: d'Ocagne, Philbert Maurice
docagne.bio: Introduced the term symmedian ('symédiane', § 558) and established fundamental properties of symmedians, the Lemoine point, and antiparallels.
works: Sur un élément du triangle rectiligne: la symédiane (1883)

euclid.name: Euclid of Alexandria
euclid.bio: Compiler of the thirteen books of the Elements, whosecompass-and-straightedge postulates and Books I–VI propositions form the explicit axiomatic bedrock of College Geometry.

euler.name: Euler, Leonhard
euler.bio: Initiated modern triangle geometry in his 1765 St. Petersburg memoir: proved the collinearity of the orthocenter H, centroid G, and circumcenter O on the Euler line (§ 201), established OI² = R² - 2Rr (§ 152), Euler's collinear four-point identity (§ 307), and quadrilateral median relations (§ 246).
works: Solutio facilis problematum quorumdam geometricorum difficillimorum (1765)

fagnano.name: Fagnano, Giovanni Francesco Toschi di
fagnano.bio: Posed and solved Fagnano's problem (1775): among all triangles inscribed in an acute triangle, the orthic triangle has minimum perimeter (§ 194).
works: Problemata quaedam ad methodum maximorum et minimorum spectantia (1775)

feuerbach.name: Feuerbach, Karl Wilhelm
feuerbach.bio: Published in 1822 at age twenty-two one of the crown jewels of elementary geometry: Feuerbach's Theorem (§ 215, § 540), proving that the nine-point circle of a triangle is internally tangent to the incircle (at the Feuerbach point X(11)) and externally tangent to the three excircles.
works: Eigenschaften einiger merkwürdigen Punkte des geradlinigen Dreiecks (1822)

fuhrmann.name: Fuhrmann, Wilhelm
fuhrmann.bio: Author of Synthetische Beweise planimetrischer Sätze (1890) and discoverer of the Fuhrmann circle and Fuhrmann triangle.

gallatly.name: Gallatly, William
gallatly.bio: Author of The Modern Geometry of the Triangle (`Gy.`, 2nd ed. 1913), frequently cited by Altshiller-Court on Lemoine, Brocard, Tucker, and orthopole theorems.
works: The Modern Geometry of the Triangle (2nd ed., 1913)

gauss.name: Gauss, Carl Friedrich
gauss.bio: Proved the collinearity of the midpoints of the three diagonals of a complete quadrilateral (the Gauss-Newton line) and studied triangle altitudes and inversion precursors.

gergonne.name: Gergonne, Joseph Diaz
gergonne.role: French Mathematician & Founder of Annales de Mathématiques
gergonne.bio: Formulated projective duality, discovered the Gergonne point X(7) where cevians to the incircle contact points concur (§ 331), and devised Gergonne's celebrated master solution to the general Problem of Apollonius using poles, polars, and the radical center (§ 517).
works: Annales de mathématiques pures et appliquées (1810–1832)
Recherche du cercle qui en touche trois autres sur une sphère ou sur un plan (1816)

grebe.name: Grebe, Ernst Wilhelm
grebe.bio: Studied the symmedian point in 1847 (hence called the Grebe point in German literature, § 572).
works: Das geradlinige Dreieck in Bezug auf die Quadrate der Perpendikel (1847)

heron.name: Heron of Alexandria
heron.bio: Formulated Heron's area formula for a triangle in terms of its semiperimeter and solved the shortest-path reflection problem on a line (§ 12).

hire.name: La Hire, Philippe de
hire.bio: Student of Desargues' projective school; author of Sectiones Conicae (1685), founder of polar reciprocity in the plane, and namesake of De la Hire's Problem (§ 292).

jacobi.name: Jacobi, Carl Friedrich Andreas
jacobi.bio: Early investigator of isogonal conjugates, Brocard angles, and triangle centers in De triangulorum rectilineorum proprietatibus (1825).
works: De triangulorum rectilineorum proprietatibus quibusdam nondum satis cognitis (1825)

johnson.name: Johnson, Roger Arthur
johnson.bio: Contemporary of Altshiller-Court and author of Modern Geometry (1929), discoverer of Johnson's three-circle theorem.
works: Modern Geometry: An Elementary Treatise on the Geometry of the Triangle and the Circle (1929)

johnson-wayne.name: Johnson, Lee Wayne
johnson-wayne.role: Professor & Head of Mathematics, Oklahoma A. and M. College
johnson-wayne.bio: Head of the Department of Mathematics at Oklahoma A. and M. College (now Oklahoma State University); acknowledged by Altshiller-Court (p. ix) for reading the 1952 manuscript with great care and contributing important suggestions and additions.
works: Introduction to Linear Algebra (with R. D. Riess & J. T. Arnold)

kimberling.name: Kimberling, Clark
kimberling.role: American Mathematician & Creator of the Encyclopedia of Triangle Centers (ETC)
kimberling.bio: Founder of the Encyclopedia of Triangle Centers (ETC), indexing X(1), X(2), ... via homogeneous trilinear and barycentric coordinates, systematically citing Altshiller-Court's College Geometry as a canonical synthetic reference.

lemoine.name: Lemoine, Émile Michel Hyacinthe
lemoine.bio: Sparked the modern geometry of the triangle with his 1873 Lyon paper on the symmedian (Lemoine) point K = X(6), Lemoine circles (first and cosine circles), Lemoine axis, and geometrography (quantitative measure of construction simplicity, Ch. X, §§ 558–596).
works: Note sur un point remarquable du plan du triangle (1873)
La Géométrographie ou l'art des constructions géométriques (1902)

lhuilier.name: L'Huilier, Simon Antoine Jean
lhuilier.bio: Author of Éléments d'analyse géométrique et d'analyse algébrique (`LHr.`, 1809), a key source for Altshiller-Court on tritangent radii, exradii identities, and geometric analysis.
works: Éléments d'analyse géométrique et d'analyse algébrique appliquées à la recherche des lieux géométriques (1809)

menelaus.name: Menelaus of Alexandria
menelaus.bio: Proved Menelaus' Theorem on collinearity of three points on the sides of a triangle via signed segment ratios (Sphaerica Book III; Ch. VI, § 310).

miquel.name: Miquel, Auguste
miquel.bio: Discovered Miquel's pivot theorem (1838) on the concurrency of circles through triangle vertices and side points, as well as the Miquel point of a complete quadrilateral.

mobius.name: Möbius, August Ferdinand
mobius.bio: Introduced homogeneous barycentric coordinates (Der barycentrische Calcul, 1827), signed areas/segments, and circular Möbius transformations.

monge.name: Monge, Gaspard
monge.role: French Geometer & Founder of the École Polytechnique
monge.bio: Creator of descriptive geometry and teacher of Carnot, Poncelet, Brianchon, and Dupin. Proved Monge's Theorem that the external centers of similitude of three circles taken in pairs are collinear (§ 405).

nagel.name: Nagel, Christian Heinrich von
nagel.bio: Investigated the tritangent centers, the Nagel point X(8) where cevians to the excircle contact points concur (§ 333), and isogonal/isotomic relations (1836).
works: Untersuchungen über die wichtigsten zum Dreiecke gehörigen Kreise (1836)

neuberg.name: Neuberg, Joseph Jean Baptiste
neuberg.bio: Co-founder (with Mansion) of Mathesis and co-architect (with Lemoine and Brocard) of modern triangle geometry; discovered the isodynamic points, Neuberg circles, and the orthopole (§ 690).
works: Sur les projections d'une droite sur les côtés d'un triangle (orthopole)

newton.name: Newton, Isaac
newton.bio: Author of Principia Mathematica and Arithmetica Universalis; proved Newton's theorem on quadrilaterals circumscribed about a circle (§ 269).

pappus.name: Pappus of Alexandria
pappus.bio: Author of the Mathematical Collection (Συναγωγή), Book VII ('Treasury of Analysis') of which codifies ancient Greek geometric Analysis and Synthesis (§ 4), preserves lemmas to Apollonius and Euclid, states the invariance of harmonic cross-ratios (§ 355), the Problem of Pappus (§ 84), and Pappus' arbelos chain (§ 545).

peaucellier.name: Peaucellier, Charles-Nicolas
peaucellier.bio: Invented Peaucellier's Cell (1864), the first exact planar linkage converting circular motion into rectilinear motion via geometric inversion (§ 533).
works: Note sur le compas composé (Nouvelles Annales, 1864 / 1873)

petersen.name: Petersen, Julius Peter Christian
petersen.bio: Author of Methods and Theories for the Solution of Problems of Geometrical Constructions (`Pt.`, 1866; English ed. 1879), the direct methodological ancestor of Altshiller-Court's Chapter I and Chapter II (Method of Loci, Similitude, Rotation, Translation).
works: Methods and Theories for the Solution of Problems of Geometrical Constructions (1879)

plato.name: Plato
plato.role: Athenian Philosopher & Founder of the Academy
plato.bio: Credited in ancient tradition with codifying the method of geometric Analysis (regressive resolution to known truths) and restricting canonical constructions to straightedge and compass.

plucker.name: Plücker, Julius
plucker.bio: Introduced trilinear coordinates, line geometry, and algebraic formulations of the radical axis and coaxal circles.

poncelet.name: Poncelet, Jean-Victor
poncelet.role: French Engineer & Architect of Projective Geometry
poncelet.bio: Wrote Traité des propriétés projectives des figures (1822), initially drafted as a prisoner of war at Saratov (1813–1814). Established continuity, ideal chords, limiting points of coaxal circles (Poncelet's coaxal theorems, Ch. VIII.G), homothecy, and (with Brianchon) the Nine-Point Circle.
works: Traité des propriétés projectives des figures (1822)

ptolemy.name: Ptolemy, Claudius
ptolemy.bio: Proved Ptolemy's Theorem in Almagest Book I, Ch. 10: in a cyclic quadrilateral, the product of the diagonals equals the sum of the products of opposite sides (§ 255; generalized by inversion in § 536).

rouche.name: Rouché, Eugène
rouche.bio: Co-author with Charles de Comberousse of Traité de géométrie (`Rouché.`, 7th ed. 1900, with Neuberg's appendix on triangle geometry), Altshiller-Court's single most frequently cited French reference.
works: Traité de géométrie (with Ch. de Comberousse, 7th ed., 1900)

servoisp.name: Servois, François-Joseph
servoisp.bio: Introduced the term 'pole' in projective geometry (1811) and studied the Wallace-Simson line independently.
works: Solutions peu connues de différens problèmes de géométrie-pratique (1804)

simson.name: Simson, Robert
simson.bio: Restorer of Euclid's Elements (1756), Euclid's Data, and Apollonius's Plane Loci (1749; cited by Altshiller-Court in § 11). Though the 'Simson line' (Ch. V, § 282) bears his name through Poncelet/Servois attribution, it was first published by William Wallace in 1799.
works: Apollonii Pergaei Locorum Planorum Libri II (1749)

spieker.name: Spieker, Theodor
spieker.bio: Author of Lehrbuch der ebenen Geometrie (1862); investigated the incircle of the medial (complementary) triangle—the Spieker circle, centered at the Spieker point X(10), center of mass of the triangle's perimeter.

steiner.name: Steiner, Jakob
steiner.bio: Regarded as the purest synthetic geometer since Apollonius. Introduced the 'power of a point' with respect to a circle (1826, Ch. VIII.E, § 412), proved fundamental theorems on the Simson line envelope (Steiner deltoid, § 299), complete quadrilaterals, inversion, the Problem of Apollonius, and the Steiner point R = X(99) on the circumcircle (§ 679).
works: Systematische Entwicklung der Abhängigkeit geometrischer Gestalten von einander (1832)

stewart.name: Stewart, Matthew
stewart.bio: Student of Robert Simson and Colin Maclaurin; published Stewart's Theorem (1746) relating the length of any cevian to the side lengths and divided base segments (Ch. VI.B, § 308).
works: Some General Theorems of Considerable Use in the Higher Parts of Mathematics (1746)

tarry.name: Tarry, Gaston
tarry.bio: Discovered the Tarry point X(98) on the circumcircle, diametrically opposite the Steiner point X(99) (§ 680).
works: Sur les figures semblablement associées à un triangle (1886)

taylor.name: Taylor, Henry Martyn
taylor.bio: Investigated the six projections of the feet of the altitudes onto the other two sides, proving they lie on a special Tucker circle: the Taylor circle (§ 689).
works: On a Six-Point Circle Connected with a Triangle (Messenger of Mathematics, 1882)

thales.name: Thales of Miletus
thales.bio: Founder of deductive Greek geometry; credited with Thales' theorem that a diameter subtends a right angle at any point on the circle (§ 11, Locus 5; Euclid III.31) and proportional intercepts on parallel lines.

thebault.name: Thébault, Victor
thebault.bio: Prolific 20th-century problemist and close correspondent of Altshiller-Court in the American Mathematical Monthly and Mathesis; contributed numerous theorems and problems to the 1952 Second Edition.

tucker.name: Tucker, Robert
tucker.role: English Mathematician & Honorary Secretary of the LMS
tucker.bio: Discovered the family of six-point Tucker circles generalizing the first Lemoine, cosine, and Taylor circles (Ch. X.F, §§ 684–689).
works: Some Properties of a Quadrilateral in a Circle and of Circles Linked with a Triangle (1885)

varignon.name: Varignon, Pierre
varignon.bio: Proved Varignon's Theorem (published posthumously 1731) that the midpoints of the sides of any quadrilateral form a parallelogram (§ 240).

viete.name: Viète, François
viete.bio: Reconstructed Apollonius's lost Tangencies in his Apollonius Gallus (1600), solving the ten cases of the Problem of Apollonius sequentially via centers of similitude and inversion precursors (§§ 506–516).

wallace.name: Wallace, William
wallace.bio: First published in Thomas Leybourn's Mathematical Repository (1799) the collinearity of the pedal projections of a circumcircle point onto the three sides of a triangle—now known as the Wallace-Simson line (§ 282).
